introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0560 History 1, June 2019, Ordinary Level, Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board). One and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: mark only one answer for each question (more than one answer scores zero for that question). The paper has three parts, all compulsory: Section A, Cameroon since 1850 (questions 1-25); Section B, Africa since 1870 excluding Cameroon (questions 26-40); Section C, World Diplomacy since 1870 (questions 41-50).
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section A: Cameroon since 1850 (questions 1-25). Section B: Africa since 1870 (excluding Cameroon) (questions 26-40). Section C: World Diplomacy since 1870 (questions 41-50).
incertitudes: Page de garde verifiee : « 0560 HISTORY 1 », JUNE 2019, ORDINARY LEVEL, Multiple Choice Question Paper, One and a half hours, « Answer ALL the 50 questions » (50 questions imprimees, aucune section a choix). Sections imprimees : A Cameroon since 1850 (Q1-25), B Africa since 1870 excluding Cameroon (Q26-40), C World Diplomacy since 1870 (Q41-50). Aucune regle de choix : regles_choix et groupes vides.
PDF avec couche texte mais lu page par page en image. Les publicites et filigranes (concourscameroon.com, logo Concours Cameroon) n'ont pas ete recopies. Aucune figure dans ce sujet : figures vide.

Fautes d'impression evidentes corrigees a la transcription (sans changer le sens) : noms propres mal ecrits (Thormahlen, Prempeh, Bissandugu, Casablanca, Clemenceau, Odumegwu), mots tronques (party, states, Pre), numerotation des options et de la question 6, placee apres la question 11 dans la mise en page imprimee ; l'option D de la Q27 n'a pas de lettre imprimee ; la Q47 imprime « 19 14 » pour 1941 (Pearl Harbour, reponse inchangee) ; la Q17 imprime « 1958s » et son option D est coupee (« P »), recopiee comme texte coupe ; la Q12 imprime « punish ... Without trial » sans complement (recopie tel quel) ; la Q15 imprime « Finest Ouandie » (Ernest Ouandie), la Q28 « Prempeh II » (Prempeh I pour les annees 1890), la Q37 « 1957s ».

La reponse retenue D (conseils legislatifs regionaux non etablis dans les annees 1990, la Constitution de 1996 les prevoyant seulement) reste la seule qui ne soit pas une reforme effective des annees 1990, mais l'enonce est imparfait.

Q3 : la description (« humane, education-minded ... native welfare ») est attribuee en general a Theodor Seitz, mais certains manuels l'appliquent a d'autres gouverneurs : question passee en OUVERTE (aucune lettre designee), options recopiees dans l'enonce, reponse visee Seitz.

Faits a faible marge d'incertitude (QCM conserves) : Q8 (accord provisoire de 1916, Picot-Milner, souvent date de mars 1916 alors que le sujet dit fevrier 1916 ; Simon et Milner sont lies a la declaration de 1919) ; Q9 (Buea, siege du Resident de la province des Cameroons) ; Q10 (1922, confirmation du Mandat, date de l'introduction officielle de l'Indirect Rule selon les manuels) ; Q17 (Endeley premier Premier en 1958, Foncha Premier a partir de 1959) ; Q22 (le sujet dit 1962 pour le premier gouvernement federal, proclame le 1er octobre 1961) ; Q23 (Green Revolution, date non precisee dans le corrige) ; Q45 (reponse A, option D imprimee incoherente). A relire par un historien avant mise en avant.
Aucun calcul numerique dans ce sujet (histoire) : rien a recalculer avec Python.

questions.enonce_markdown: A European power whose naval presence and consular activities helped in solving trade disputes between European traders and Cameroon Middle men between 1841 to 1883?
questions.corrige_markdown: Before the German annexation of 1884, the coast of Cameroon was dominated by British influence. Royal Navy ships of the West Africa Squadron patrolled the coast (after the abolition of the slave trade) and British consuls resident for the Bights of Benin and Biafra (and later at Fernando Po) settled quarrels between European traders and the Duala middlemen, for example through the Courts of Equity set up in Douala and the "comey" (trade-tax) agreements. France had no comparable presence on the Cameroon coast then, Germany only arrived in 1884 and Portugal's interests had long since moved away. **Answer: A.**
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the trading firms that were established by the German traders in 1868 and 1875 respectively in Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Hamburg merchant Carl Woermann opened a trading house at Douala in 1868, and the firm Jantzen and Thormählen (also of Hamburg) followed in 1875. These two firms were the leading German traders on the coast before annexation and pressed Bismarck to protect their interests. "Ambas Bay" is a place, not a firm, and R.W. King was a British firm. The order 1868 then 1875 therefore gives Woermann then Jantzen and Thormählen. **Answer: B.**
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

choix.texte: Carl Woermann and Jantzen and Thormählen
Jantzen and Thormählen and Ambas Bay

questions.enonce_markdown:
Question 3 is based on this description of a German Colonial Official: "Humane, (Kind-hearted) education-minded and a strong advocate for native welfare". Which German Governor best suits this description?

*Options as printed:* A) Von Zimmerer   B) Von Soden   C) Theodore Seitz   D) Karl Ebermaier
questions.corrige_markdown:
The German governors of Kamerun were Von Soden (1885-1891), Von Zimmerer (1891-1895), Von Puttkamer (1895-1907), Theodor Seitz (1907-1910), Gleim (1910-1912) and Ebermaier (1912-1916). Von Zimmerer and Von Puttkamer are remembered for harsh treatment of Africans, forced labour and punitive expeditions, so they do not fit the description. Among the remaining names, Theodor Seitz is the one most often presented in Cameroonian history textbooks as the more humane governor who showed concern for African welfare and for schooling, but the description could also be applied to other governors by some authors.

**Intended answer: C (Theodore Seitz).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which economic measure was taken after 1906 to consolidate German authority over the resources in the territory?
questions.corrige_markdown: From 1906 the Germans began building railways (the Northern Railway from Douala towards Nkongsamba, then the Central or Midland line towards Yaounde) and roads, to carry plantation and forest products (rubber, palm produce, cocoa, timber) from the interior to the ports and to control the resources. A colonial force (the Schutztruppe) and military stations belong to the earlier conquest phase of the 1880s and 1890s, and primary schools are a social measure, not an economic one. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Construction of roads and railways to open up the interior

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the Duala traditional ruler that planned a national resistance against German colonial rule and was executed in 1914?
questions.corrige_markdown: Rudolf Duala Manga Bell, paramount chief of the Bell people of Douala, opposed the German plan to expropriate Duala land and move the Duala inland (1910-1914). He sent appeals to the Reichstag and tried to obtain support from other chiefs. At the outbreak of the First World War the Germans accused him of treason and hanged him in August 1914 together with his secretary Ngoso Din. Lock Priso (Bele Bele) resisted the annexation of 1884 and Martin Paul Samba (the printed "Marlin" is a misprint) was a southern leader executed in 1914 as well, but the planner of the Duala national resistance was Duala Manga Bell. **Answer: A.**
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: Which missionary body established a mission station at Marienberg (Edea) in the 1890s to promote the Catholic church in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Pallottines (the Society of the Catholic Apostolate, German Catholic missionaries) arrived in Cameroon in 1890 and opened stations in the south and along the coast, among them Marienberg near Edea. The London Missionary Society and the Basel Mission were Protestant societies, and the Holy Ghost Fathers (Spiritans) only took over Catholic work after the Germans left, from 1916. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Cameroon Traditional ruler who after the defeat of the Germans in 1916 went on exile to Spanish Equatorial Guinea.
questions.corrige_markdown: Charles Atangana, the Ewondo paramount chief at Yaounde who had been a loyal ally of the Germans, withdrew with the retreating German forces to Spanish Guinea in 1916 and returned to Yaounde in 1919, when the French restored him to office. Fon Galega I of Bali and Sultan Njoya of Bamum were not exiled to Spanish Guinea at that time (Njoya was exiled by the French in 1931). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The French official directly involved in the provisional partitioning of Cameroon with the British Government in February 1916 was
questions.corrige_markdown: The first provisional division of the conquered German Kamerun between Britain and France was negotiated in London in early 1916 between the French diplomat Georges Picot and the British Lord Milner (the Picot-Milner arrangement, dated March 1916 in many books). Alfred Milner and Lancelot Oliphant were British, and Henri Simon, French Minister of the Colonies, is linked to the later Milner-Simon Declaration of July 1919, the definitive partition. **Answer: D.**
themes: partition of cameroon after world war one

questions.enonce_markdown: Which town served as the administrative headquarters of the Resident in British Southern Cameroons during the Mandate period?
questions.corrige_markdown: Buea, the former German colonial capital at the foot of Mount Cameroon, was the seat of the British Resident for the Cameroons Province, administered as part of Nigeria. Victoria, Mamfe and Bamenda (Bali was a local centre) were divisional centres under District Officers, not the seat of the Resident. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following official dates was the British policy of Indirect Rule introduced in Southern Cameroons during the Mandate period?
questions.corrige_markdown: The League of Nations Mandate over British Cameroons was confirmed in 1922, and the British then administered the territory with the Nigerian system of Indirect Rule through Native Authorities and chiefs. 1916 was the year of the military conquest and the provisional partition, and 1920 and 1924 do not mark the official introduction of the policy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Question 11 is based on this statement and is historically correct: Opposition to French Colonial Policies led to his exile to Yaounde in the early 1930s. This statement best refers to which of the following Cameroonian traditional rulers during the Mandate period?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sultan Ibrahim Njoya of the Bamum kingdom clashed with the French administration, which restricted his powers, closed his schools and curbed his revenues. In 1931 he was banished to Yaounde, where he died in 1933. Charles Atangana was a favoured chief of the French and the other names do not fit this exile. **Answer: D.**
themes: french rule in cameroon under the mandate

questions.enonce_markdown: The official name given to a number of provisions in the French criminal code that permitted French colonial officials to arbitrarily punish without trial was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Indigenat (the code de l'indigenat) was a set of special rules by which administrators could punish "natives" (fines, imprisonment, forced labour) without a regular trial. The prestation was the labour obligation, the corvee was forced unpaid labour, and mise en valeur was the policy of developing colonial resources. **Answer: B.**
themes: french rule in cameroon under the mandate

questions.enonce_markdown: The most important political effect on the people of Southern Cameroons after the Second World War from after 1945 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: After 1945 the United Nations replaced the League of Nations, and in 1946 the British Cameroons passed from Mandate to Trusteeship, so Southern Cameroons became a UN Trust Territory administered by Britain. This was a political change. The CDC (set up in 1946-1947 on former German plantations) was an economic body, and neither "protectorate of the UNO" nor self-governing status was granted in 1945. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Southern Cameroons became a UN Trust Territory
Southern Cameroons became a Protectorate of the UNO
an agro-industrial corporation called the CDC was established
Southern Cameroons was granted the status of a self-governing territory by the U.N.O

questions.enonce_markdown: The two pressure groups in Southern Cameroons that merged in 1953 to form the first political party, the Kamerun National Congress, were...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Cameroons National Federation (CNF, led by E.M.L. Endeley) and the Kamerun United National Congress (KUNC) merged in 1953 to form the Kamerun National Congress (KNC). The Cameroons Youth League (CYL) and the Cameroon Welfare Union (the printed CWU) were earlier pressure groups that did not form this merger. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the UPC leader in the Bassa region that led a revolt against the French as a result of rigged elections in the 1950s?
questions.corrige_markdown: Ruben Um Nyobe, Secretary-General of the Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC), came from the Bassa country. After the UPC was banned in 1955 he led the resistance in the Sanaga-Maritime (Bassa) region and was killed by French forces in 1958. Kingue, Ouandie and Moumie were other UPC leaders, but the Bassa leader was Um Nyobe. ("Finest Ouandie" is printed in option B; the leader's name is Ernest Ouandie.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The French High Commissioner of the Republic who was specifically given the mission by his home government to destroy the UPC political party in Cameroon in the 1950s was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Roland Pré was High Commissioner from 1954 to 1956 and was sent by Paris with the task of crushing the UPC, which was banned in July 1955 after the May 1955 riots. Jean Ramadier (1950-1954) and Xavier Torre (the printed "Torres") were other High Commissioners and Richard Brunot is not the officer given this mission. **Answer: B.**
themes: upc and french repression in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The Cameroon nationalist leader who became the first Premier of Southern Cameroons in the 1958s was...
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1958 the London constitutional conference gave Southern Cameroons full regional status with a Premier in place of the earlier Leader of Government Business, and E.M.L. Endeley, leader of the KNC, held the office first. J.N. Foncha (KNDP) won the elections of January 1959 and became Premier after him. S.T. Muna was a minister, not Premier. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: [option text cut off in the printed paper]

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following Constitutional reforms carried out by the British government finally gave Southern Cameroons a full regional status in 1959?
questions.corrige_markdown: Richards (1946-47), Macpherson (1951-52) and Lyttelton (1954) were successive steps: Lyttelton gave Southern Cameroons a quasi-federal status in 1954. Full regional status was the result of the London constitutional conference of 1957-1958, after which the territory got its own Premier, House of Chiefs and a regional government before the 1959 elections. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason why Mbida's government collapsed in 1958 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Andre-Marie Mbida, Prime Minister of French Cameroon from 1957, opposed immediate independence and the reunification of the two Cameroons and was close to the French authorities, which cost him the support of the Assembly and his own coalition and led to his fall in February 1958. He was a hostile opponent of the UPC, not its collaborator, and he was himself a Catholic. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: his rejection of the policy of immediate independence and reunification
his policy of collaboration with the UPC
his refusal to form a coalition government with Ahidjo
lack of support from the Catholic church

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following political leaders and his party took over government in French Cameroon in February 1958?
questions.corrige_markdown: After Mbida's resignation, Ahmadou Ahidjo, leader of the Union Camerounaise (UC), became Prime Minister in February 1958 and led French Cameroon to independence on 1 January 1960. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The last Prime Minister of the state of West Cameroon who witnessed its collapse in 1972 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: West Cameroon's Prime Ministers were J.N. Foncha (1961-1965), A.N. Jua (1965-1968) and S.T. Muma (1968-1972). The federal structure was abolished after the referendum of 20 May 1972, which created the United Republic of Cameroon, so Muma was the last. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following Southern Cameroons political leaders and his party joined with Ahmadou Ahidjo and his political party (UC) to form the first federal government in 1962 in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: J.N. Foncha and his Kamerun National Democratic Party (KNDP), which had campaigned for reunification, joined Ahidjo's Union Camerounaise in the federal arrangement that began on 1 October 1961 and became the Federal Republic's Vice-President. Endeley's CPNC favoured integration with Nigeria, and Ndeh Ntumazah's One Kamerun (O.K.) was a radical opposition party. The question prints 1962 for the date of the first federal government, but the Federal Republic was proclaimed in October 1961. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The famous campaign carried out by the Ahidjo government to increase agricultural production in Cameroon in the 1970s was known as...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Green Revolution campaign of the Ahidjo government aimed at raising food and export crop production and at making the country self-sufficient in food. "Operation Feed the Nation" belongs to Nigeria (1976), and the Operation Sahel Vert was a tree-planting scheme against desertification in the north. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: All the following reforms were taken by the Biya regime to reduce ANGLOPHONE agitation and demonstrations in the 1990s except one. Identify the exception.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the 1990s the government appointed Anglophone Prime Ministers (Simon Achidi Achu in 1992, Peter Mafany Musonge in 1996), created the Cameroon GCE Board in 1993 (so that Anglophones would control their own examinations) and opened the University of Buea in 1993 on the Anglo-Saxon model. The 1996 Constitution provided for regions with councils, but regional legislative councils were not set up in the Anglophone regions in the 1990s, so it is the exception. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Appointment of Anglophone Prime Ministers in his governments
Creation of the Cameroon GCE Board and establishment of an Anglo-Saxon University in Buea
Establishment of an Anglo-Saxon university in Buea
Establishment of Regional Legislative Councils in the Anglophone regions

questions.enonce_markdown: To which of the following international organisations has Cameroon provided two Secretaries-General in the 1970s?
questions.corrige_markdown: Two Cameroonians led the Organisation of African Unity as Administrative Secretary-General in the 1970s: William Eteki Mboumoua (1972-1974) and Nzo Ekangaki (1974-1978). Cameroon provided no Secretary-General of the UN or of the Commonwealth, and the African Union only replaced the OAU in 2002. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which European trader and his company known as the Royal Niger Company through its activities annexed Nigeria for the British in the 1870s and 1880s?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sir George Taubman Goldie united the British trading firms on the Niger into the National African Company (1879), which became the Royal Niger Company after the royal charter of 1886. Its treaties with local rulers and its trade monopoly gave Britain its claim to the Niger basin at the Berlin Conference. Rhodes worked in southern Africa, Stanley in the Congo for Leopold II and Karl Peters in East Africa for Germany. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The pair of European colonial powers that did Not have colonies in Africa before 1870 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Before 1870 Britain (Cape, Sierra Leone, Gold Coast, Lagos), France (Algeria, Senegal), Portugal (Angola, Mozambique, Guinea) and Spain (small coastal posts) already held African territory. Italy and Germany only became unified nations in 1861 and 1871 and acquired African colonies in the 1880s. Option D wrongly includes Portugal. (The letter D is missing in the printed paper for this option.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Below is a list of African leaders who were nation builders between the 1870s and 1890s. Select the one who challenged the French invasion of his territory in West Africa.
questions.corrige_markdown: Samori Toure, founder of the Mandinka (Wassoulou) empire, fought the French for almost two decades until his capture in 1898. Menelik II resisted Italy in East Africa, the Asante king resisted the British and King Jaja of Opobo was removed by the British. The paper prints "Prempeh II"; the Asante king of the 1890s was Prempeh I. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The European colonial policy that considered Africans as "immature, ignorant and unable to govern themselves" was called...
questions.corrige_markdown: Paternalism treated Africans as children who had to be guided and protected by Europeans. Assimilation aimed to turn Africans into Frenchmen, Indirect Rule used traditional rulers, and the Indigenat was a legal code of punishments. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of the following African territories was the British policy of Indirect Rule most successful?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lord Lugard introduced Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria, where the Hausa-Fulani emirate system of chiefs, courts and tax collection was already organised, so the policy worked best there. In Kenya it fitted poorly because of settlers and decentralised societies, and in the Gold Coast and Sierra Leone it was less successful. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which battle ended the struggle for political control between Abyssinia and Italy in the Horn of Africa in 1896?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Battle of Adowa (Adwa) on 1 March 1896 gave Emperor Menelik II a decisive victory over the Italian army, and Italy had to recognise Ethiopian independence in the Treaty of Addis Ababa. Ucciali (Wuchale) was the treaty of 1889 that caused the dispute, Bissandugu was the capital of Samori Toure, who signed a treaty with France there in 1887 and Wal Wal was a border incident of 1934. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The French colonial policy used to govern their West African territories was...

*Options as printed:* A) Paternalism   B) Assimilation   C) Indirect Rule   D) Direct Rule
questions.corrige_markdown:
France governed its West African territories under a policy of Assimilation (turning Africans into French citizens through French language, education and culture) applied through Direct Rule, with French officials and appointed chiefs taking orders from the governor. Paternalism and Indirect Rule are not the French approach. Since both Assimilation and Direct Rule describe the French system, the question has two defensible answers.

**Intended answer: B (Assimilation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The main political effect of the First World War on Africa was that...
questions.corrige_markdown: African soldiers and carriers who fought in Europe and in the African campaigns saw that Europeans could be defeated and divided, and learnt ideas of self-determination, which fed the later nationalist movements: a political effect. Urbanisation is a social effect, only the former German colonies became Mandates, and the printed option D is not a main political effect. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the war led to the urbanisation of Africa
Africans came in contact with European political ideas
All African territories came under Mandate rule
the harsh German colonial policy of Paternalism came to an end

questions.enonce_markdown: Which independent African territory was liberated from Italian occupation in 1941 by the Allied forces during the Second World War?
questions.corrige_markdown: Italy occupied the independent Abyssinia (Ethiopia) in 1935-36 and the country was liberated in 1941 by British and Commonwealth forces with Ethiopian patriots; Emperor Haile Selassie returned to Addis Ababa. Libya and Eritrea were Italian colonies, not independent states, and Egypt was never occupied by Italy. **Answer: B.**
themes: impact of world war two on africa

questions.enonce_markdown: The African city that hosted an important wartime conference in 1943 where Churchill and Roosevelt met to plan the Allied conquest of Italy was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Casablanca Conference (Morocco) of January 1943 brought Churchill and Roosevelt together; they decided to invade Sicily and then Italy and to demand the unconditional surrender of the Axis. The printed option reads "Cassablanca". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The African Nationalist leader who was accused by the British for leading the Mau-Mau movement in Kenya from 1952 to 1961 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The British blamed Jomo Kenyatta, president of the Kenya African Union, for leading Mau Mau, arrested him in 1952 and imprisoned him after the Kapenguria trial (1953). He denied the charge and became the first Prime Minister and then President of independent Kenya. Mboya and Odinga were other Kenyan politicians and Nyerere was Tanzanian. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first British colony in West Africa to experience a peaceful decolonisation through constitutional process leading to independence in the 1957s was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Gold Coast, led by Kwame Nkrumah and his CPP, became independent as Ghana on 6 March 1957 after a series of constitutional steps and elections. Nigeria followed in 1960, Sierra Leone in 1961 and The Gambia in 1965. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Question 38 is based on this quotation made by a South African nationalist and statesman on the occasion of his country achieving Black majority rule in 1994. "Never, never and never again shall it be that this beautiful land will again experience the oppression of one by another..." Identify the South African statesman who made this statement.
questions.corrige_markdown: These words come from the inauguration speech of Nelson Mandela, first President of the democratic South Africa, in May 1994. Mugabe was Zimbabwe's leader, Mbeki succeeded Mandela in 1999 and De Klerk was the last apartheid-era President. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the Biafran (Ibo) secessionist leader during the Nigerian Civil War of the 1960s?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lt-Col Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu proclaimed the Republic of Biafra in May 1967 and led it until its defeat in January 1970. Yakubu Gowon was the federal head of state, and Murtala Mohammed and Olusegun Obasanjo were federal officers. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first Summit of the O.A.U was held in 1963 at...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Organisation of African Unity was founded at the summit of independent African states held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in May 1963, and the Organisation set up its headquarters there. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following European powers was the most industrialized nation in the world by the mid 1870s?
questions.corrige_markdown: Britain was the first industrial nation and, in the mid 1870s, still led the world in coal, iron, steel, textiles and shipping, the "workshop of the world". Germany only overtook Britain in steel and several other sectors later, towards 1900. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bismarck's main aim of isolating France between 1870 and 1890 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Germany took Alsace and Lorraine from France in 1871. Bismarck feared a French war of revenge to recover them, so he kept France without allies through the Dreikaiserbund, the Dual Alliance with Austria (1879) and the Triple Alliance (1882). German unification was already achieved in 1871, and relations with Austria were a means, not the aim. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: to prevent France from taking back Alsace and Lorraine
to achieve the unification of Germany
to improve relations between Germany and Austria
to make France develop interest in the Balkans.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Alliance System that was formed to check the ambitions of Germany and Austria in the Balkans that led to the outbreak of the First World War was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Triple Entente (France, Russia and Britain, formed by 1907) faced the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy) and stood against the German and Austro-Hungarian ambitions in the Balkans, where Russia backed Serbia. The Triple Alliance and Dual Alliance were the German-Austrian camp itself, and the Entente Cordiale (1904) was only an Anglo-French agreement. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main economic effect of the First World War on Europe that led to political crisis in the 1920s and 1930s was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The war destroyed industries and ran up huge debts and reparations, producing runaway inflation (Germany, 1923) and then mass unemployment in the Great Depression. This economic distress weakened democratic governments and helped extremist movements. New states and weak democracies are political results, and the rise of Hitler and Mussolini is a political consequence of the crisis, not the economic effect itself. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: the creation of new states in Europe
the rise of Hitler and Mussolini

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest challenge to the Principle of Collective Security in the 1920s and 1930s was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Collective security meant that members would act together against an aggressor. It failed because dictators (Japan in Manchuria in 1931, Italy in Ethiopia in 1935, Germany under Hitler) attacked other states and the League could not stop them. Treaty breaking and withdrawals were results of this aggression, and option D is garbled in the printed paper. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the withdrawal of member states from the League
The USA in the outbreak to create Depression in USA

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was a manifestation of the Cold War in Europe after 1945?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Berlin Blockade (June 1948 to May 1949), when the USSR cut land access to West Berlin and the Allies answered with the airlift, was the first major Cold War crisis in Europe. The Yalta Conference took place during the war, the Korean War was in Asia and the Cuban Missile Crisis in the Caribbean. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which event caused the U.S.A. to become actively involved in the Second World War in 1941?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Japanese surprise air attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor (Hawaii) on 7 December 1941 brought the USA into the war. The events in A, B and C happened earlier and the USA stayed neutral. The year is printed as "19 14" in the paper, which is a misprint for 1941. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The League of Nations was the brainchild of
questions.corrige_markdown: US President Woodrow Wilson proposed the League in his Fourteen Points (January 1918), as the last point, and pressed for it at the Paris Peace Conference. Clemenceau, Smuts and Lloyd George took part but the idea is credited to Wilson (the USA itself never joined). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which international agency fights to stop the spread of diseases and epidemics in the world since 1948?
questions.corrige_markdown: The World Health Organization (WHO), a UN specialised agency created in 1948, works against diseases and epidemics. FAO deals with food and agriculture, UNESCO with education, science and culture and UNICEF with children. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which International Organization is in charge of promoting Football as a sport that fosters peace and friendship among peoples of the world?
questions.corrige_markdown: FIFA (Federation Internationale de Football Association, founded in 1904) governs world football and organises the World Cup. The IOC runs the Olympic Games, and UEFA and CAF are continental bodies for Europe and Africa. **Answer: B.**
